## Content-quality rubric
Major/minor describe task-quality defects and do not determine operational incident severity.

| Dimension | Major defect | Minor defect | Acceptable / no automatic penalty |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Factual accuracy | Error changes the central conclusion or actionable answer | Nonessential background error without that effect | Accurate paraphrase or an immaterial stylistic difference |
| Instruction adherence | Explicit required format/structure is missing | Limited violation of an actual secondary requirement | A stylistic choice that violates no requirement |
| Citation support | Fabricated reference or materially unsupported attribution | A limited citation-detail error where the source and support remain identifiable | A valid source that supports the claim |
| Preference | Identify a meaningful benefit; grade underlying defects separately | Do not manufacture a defect to break a tie | No meaningful quality difference supports a tie |

An inaccessible link needs a verification note; lack of access alone does not establish the error grade of the claim.

## Ties and preferences

### Q: How much improvement is needed to avoid a tie?
The difference must offer a meaningful benefit to the user. Cosmetic phrasing alone usually does not. Explain that benefit; otherwise a tie can be appropriate.

### Q: QA is reversing ties on similar pairs. What should I do?
Share the pairs, relevant prompt constraints and both rationales for calibration. Check whether the cases are actually comparable. An answer to one pair should not be generalized without matching its scope.

## Factual errors

### Q: What counts as a significant factual error?
An error that changes the central conclusion or the answer the user would act on. A nonessential background detail with no effect on the recommendation is minor.

Record that the citation could not be verified. A failed URL alone does not prove the claim is false. Distinguish access failure from an unsupported attribution or fabricated reference.

k:rp-format-rule-rejected@1.0:59d718d7.excerpt:
[PRIOR RECORD (advice_review; decision_status: tl_rejected; execution_status: not_executed; outcome_status: no_policy_change) - history, not a standing rule.]
# TL rejects a universal JSON-first preference rule

## Suggested advice
A simulated prior Advisor card proposed: “Whenever the prompt requires JSON, prefer the JSON-formatted response over prose.”

## TL response
Alex rejected this as a universal rule. A required format violation is a real instruction-adherence defect, but format compliance alone does not establish the better response when the other candidate has a different factual defect.

The review packet lacked the complete prompt and both responses. Request those materials and score the dimensions separately. A case-specific decision may be possible once they are available; this review makes no such decision.

## Consequence
No general JSON-first rule was approved, posted or added to the FAQ. Rejection also does not create a prose-first rule. Keep genuinely unresolved trade-offs open for TL confirmation.
